label: Forestdb (index storage engine)
type: the index storage engine that implements `standard` index storage in COMMUNITY Edition. A LEVEL-3 term - see concepts/index-storage-stack.json. The only member of the family with a level below it: Forestdb alone has a write mode (Circular or Append-only). Not a KV engine; see storage-engine:plasma's warning.
recurrence_note: Three files, but the honest number is nearer two, and the reason is a limit of the round's own instrument. The three are storage-modes.md, alterindex.md and altervectorindex.md - and the last two score 0.69 similarity over 248 and 257 body lines. shared-source.py does not cluster them for TWO reasons at once: 0.69 is below the 0.75 threshold, and the test also requires a matching basename, which `alterindex` and `altervectorindex` do not have. This is the docstring's 'a renamed twin is invisible' limit, met in the wild on the round's first look, with BOTH of the test's conditions failing independently. Promoted anyway - two independent sources is the bar and storage-modes.md plus the alterindex pair clears it - but recorded so the 3 is not read as three authors. The clone relationship is already filed, from an earlier round and for a different reason: docs-issues/server-altervectorindex-inherits-wrong-version-gates records that altervectorindex.md is 'a near-verbatim clone of alterindex.md' and has inherited its version gates wholesale. That issue is about wrong version facts; the consequence noted here is that the clone also inflates recurrence, which nobody had connected to it.
note: PROMOTED. Community Edition only: 'In Couchbase Server Community Edition, standard index storage is supported by the Forestdb storage engine.' Together with the Plasma sentence this is the one-to-many map that proves a setting value is not an engine. Two further things this record must not be read as saying. First, Forestdb is not deprecated as far as this corpus states - no page in 593 records says so, which is a notable absence for an engine most Couchbase practitioners would describe that way, and the registry does not get to import that from outside the documentation. Second, Circular and Append-only are Forestdb's write modes and are NOT promoted: two words on one page, and the level is recorded in concepts/index-storage-stack.json instead.
relates_to_competency_question: Which storage engine actually backs my indexes, and is that something I chose?
